cases.sentence: Наташа широко ___, как будто она хотела перехватить всякий устремленный на нее взгляд, беспокойно оглядывалась на всех и старалась казаться такою же, какою она была всегда.
cases.explain: «раскрытыми глазами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Morning came with its cares and bustle. Everyone got up and began to move about and talk, dressmakers came again. Márya Dmítrievna appeared, and they were called to breakfast. Natásha kept looking uneasily at everybody with wide-open eyes, as if wishing to intercept every glance directed toward her, and tried to appear the same as usual.

cases.sentence: После завтрака Марья Дмитриевна (это было лучшее время ее), сев на свое кресло, подозвала к себе Наташу и ___.
cases.explain: «старого графа» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: After breakfast, which was her best time, Márya Dmítrievna sat down in her armchair and called Natásha and the count to her.

cases.explain: «истинная правда» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That is perfectly true. And I am sorry I went to see him and took her,” said the old count.

cases.sentence: — Я и жалею, что к нему ездил и ее возил, — сказал ___.
cases.explain: «старый граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That is perfectly true. And I am sorry I went to see him and took her,” said the old count.

cases.sentence: Он больной и ___, которого надо извинять; но он добр, великодушен и будет любить ту, которая сделает счастье его сына».
cases.explain: «старый человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Do not think, however,” she wrote, “that my father is ill-disposed toward you. He is an invalid and an old man who must be forgiven; but he is good and magnanimous and will love her who makes his son happy.” Princess Márya went on to ask Natásha to fix a time when she could see her again.

cases.sentence: Прочтя письмо, Наташа села к ___, чтобы написать ответ: «Chère princesse»,[555] Милая княжна, быстро, механически написала она и остановилась.
cases.explain: «письменному столу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: After reading the letter Natásha sat down at the writing table to answer it. “Dear Princess,” she wrote in French quickly and mechanically, and then paused. What more could she write after all that had happened the evening before? “Yes, yes! All that has happened, and now all is changed,” she thought as she sat with the letter she had begun before her. “Must I break off with him? Must I really? That’s awful …” and to escape from these dreadful thoughts she went to Sónya and began sorting patterns with her.

cases.sentence: Прочтя письмо, Наташа села к письменному столу, чтобы написать ответ: «Chère princesse»,[555] ___, быстро, механически написала она и остановилась.

cases.sentence: И чтобы не думать этих ___, она пошла к Соне и с ней вместе стала разбирать узоры.
cases.explain: «страшных мыслей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: After reading the letter Natásha sat down at the writing table to answer it. “Dear Princess,” she wrote in French quickly and mechanically, and then paused. What more could she write after all that had happened the evening before? “Yes, yes! All that has happened, and now all is changed,” she thought as she sat with the letter she had begun before her. “Must I break off with him? Must I really? That’s awful …” and to escape from these dreadful thoughts she went to Sónya and began sorting patterns with her.

cases.sentence: — Барышня, — шопотом с ___ сказала девушка, входя в комнату.
cases.explain: «таинственным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Please, Miss!” whispered a maid entering the room with a mysterious air. “A man told me to give you this—” and she handed Natásha a letter. “Only, for Christ’s sake …” the girl went on, as Natásha, without thinking, mechanically broke the seal and read a love letter from Anatole, of which, without taking in a word, she understood only that it was a letter from him—from the man she loved. Yes, she loved him, or else how could that have happened which had happened? And how could she have a love letter from him in her hand?

cases.explain: «другого выхода» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Since yesterday evening my fate has been sealed; to be loved by you or to die. There is no other way for me,” the letter began. Then he went on to say that he knew her parents would not give her to him—for this there were secret reasons he could reveal only to her—but that if she loved him she need only say the word yes, and no human power could hinder their bliss. Love would conquer all. He would steal her away and carry her off to the ends of the earth.

cases.sentence: «Да, да, я люблю его!» думала Наташа, перечитывая в двадцатый раз письмо и отыскивая какой-то особенный ___ в каждом его слове.
cases.explain: «глубокий смысл» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, yes! I love him!” thought Natásha, reading the letter for the twentieth time and finding some peculiarly deep meaning in each word of it.
